'''Nakatsu Daijingu''' (中津大神宮) and '''Nakatsu Shrine''' (中津神社) are Shinto shrines located in Ni-no-chō, {{ill|Nakatsu, Ōita|en|Nakatsu, Ōita|qid=Q861221|lt=Nakatsu|1=Nakatsu, Ōita}}, {{ill|Ōita Prefecture|en|Ōita Prefecture|qid=Q133924|lt=Ōita Prefecture|1=Ōita Prefecture}}. Both shrines hold the status of former village shrines under the pre-modern shrine Ranking system.

== History ==
=== Nakatsu Castle in the Meiji Restoration Period ===
[[File:中津城Tenshu.jpg|thumb|right|Nakatsu Castle’s reconstructed tenshu]]

In August 1863 (Bunkyū 3), the southern part of Nakatsu Castle’s main keep was developed into the “Pine Palace,” which housed princesses returning from the domain’s Edo residence.<ref name="Pine Palace Info">Informational Signboard “Pine Palace,” Nakatsu City, Historical Society of Nakatsu</ref> After the 1871 (Meiji 4) {{ill|Abolition of the han system|en|Abolition of the han system|qid=Q331905|lt=Abolition of the han system|1=Abolition of the han system}}, the Pine Palace was repurposed as the Nakatsu City Hall under the {{ill|Kokura Prefecture|en|Kokura Prefecture|qid=Q5765997|lt=Kokura Prefecture|1=Kokura Prefecture}} administration and later served as the Nakatsu Branch of Ōita Prefecture.<ref name="Pine Palace Info"/>

During the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|qid=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion|1=Satsuma Rebellion}}, dissatisfied samurai from the former Nakatsu Domain formed the {{ill|Nakatsu Corps|ja|中津隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsu Corps|1=Q11366514|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11366514}} and burned the Pine Palace on March 31, 1877.<ref name="Pine Palace Info"/>

=== Establishment of Nakatsu Daijingu and Nakatsu Shrine ===
[[File:Nakatsu Daijingu ac (2).jpg|thumb|Torii of Nakatsu Shrines]]

Nakatsu Daijingu was established in 1881 (Meiji 14) as the Buzen Shrine Association, enshrining spirits from {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}. Initially, it served as a center for pilgrims from the Buzen region, distributing {{ill|Jingū taima|en|Jingū taima|qid=Q11589469|lt=Ise talismans|1=Jingū taima}} and calendars.<ref name="Nakatsu Daijingu About"/> It underwent several name changes before being renamed Nakatsu Daijingu in 1946.

Nakatsu Shrine was established in 1883 (Meiji 16) on the former site of the Pine Palace. It consolidated deities from six local shrines, including Rokusho Shrine, Maruyama Shrine, and Hachiman Ōe Shrine.<ref name="Nakatsu Shrine About"/>

== Grounds ==
[[File:Nakatsu Castle Park ac (2).jpg|thumb|160px|“Nakatsu Corps Memorial”]]

The grounds feature several notable monuments:<ref name="Grounds Overview">[http://nakatsudaijinguu.jp/keidai.html Grounds Overview] Nakatsu Daijingu</ref>
* “Nakatsu Corps Memorial” - Dedicated to the Nakatsu Corps, which rose during the Satsuma Rebellion.
* “Centennial Memorial of Nakatsu Corps”<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* “Kyōji Shinmei Monument”<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* “Imperial Accession Memorial”<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* “Russo-Japanese War Shell Monument”<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|en|Matsuo Bashō|qid=Q5676|lt=Matsuo Bashō|1=Matsuo Bashō}} Haiku Monument<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* Kii Shrine - Enshrines {{ill|Kii Tadamune|ja|城井鎮房|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Tadamune|1=Utsunomiya Shigefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11425978}}, a lord assassinated at Nakatsu Castle by {{ill|Kuroda Nagamasa|en|Kuroda Nagamasa|qid=Q950496|lt=Kuroda Nagamasa|1=Kuroda Nagamasa}}.<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* Senjō Shrine - Dedicated to 45 retainers of Kii Tadamune.<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>
* Kotohira Shrine - Dedicated to the deity of maritime safety.<ref name="Grounds Overview"/>

== Festivals ==
{{main|{{ill|Nakatsu Gion Festival|ja|中津祇園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsu Gion Festival|qq=}}}}
Nakatsu Gion, held annually in late July, features {{ill|Mikoshi|en|Mikoshi|qid=Q979940|lt=Mikoshi|1=Mikoshi}} and {{ill|Matsuri float|en|Matsuri float|qid=Q11470974|lt=Yamahoko|1=Matsuri float}} processions. The festival is centered on Yasaka Shrine (a subsidiary of {{ill|Yamami Shrine|ja|闇無濱神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 闇無浜神社|1=Kuranashihama Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q130214370}}) and Nakatsu Shrine, collectively known as Nakatsu Gion. Records trace its origins to 1430 (Eikyō 2). Nakatsu Gion is considered one of the “Three Great Festivals of Buzen” and “Three Major Gion Festivals of Ōita Prefecture.”<ref name="Nakatsu Gion History">[https://nakatsu-gion.com/rekishi/ About Nakatsu Gion] Nakatsu Gion</ref> It was designated a {{ill|Ōita Prefecture Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|大分県選択無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōita Prefecture Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1962 (Shōwa 37) and upgraded to a Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 2004.<ref name="#1">[https://www.city-nakatsu.jp/doc/2011100115127/ Prefectural Cultural Properties] Nakatsu City</ref>
